extract: A typed copy of the columns in COLUMNS for every present fiscal year: federal_action_obligation as DECIMAL(38,6) (the AMT expression of src/analyses_v2.py), action_date as a date, the vendor as the VENDOR expression and the placeholder flag as the MFA expression. Text is kept as published.
segment: As in src/analyses_v2.py. The awarding agency code as recorded x product or service code x fiscal year. A blank product code is its own value.
vendor: As in src/analyses_v2.py. recipient_parent_uei, or recipient_uei when the parent is blank. Rows with both blank form one vendor, '(no ID)'.
proposed_handling: Variant V1 of src/eda/base_tables.py on the shivram-eda branch. Each reversal pair in PAIRS keeps the pair's net on its first listed row and its second row is set to zero. The two rows in MINT_KEYS, rows matching MFA and the vendor '(no ID)' are left out.
hhi: As hhi() in src/analyses_v2.py. 10,000 x the sum of squared shares, where a share is a vendor's dollars divided by the summed dollars of vendors with positive dollars in the segment. A segment with no such vendor is unscored.
bands: HHI bands as in src/concentration_prelim.py: 1,500 or less; above 1,500 to 1,800; above 1,800 to 2,500; above 2,500, two or more vendors; 10,000, one vendor, plus 'unscored'. Each band includes its upper bound. A segment changes band when its band differs between two runs, a segment missing from one run counting as unscored there.
share_above_2500: The summed net (under the proposed handling) of segments whose HHI is strictly above 2,500, divided by the summed net of all rows under the proposed handling that year, in percent. Civilian: the same over every awarding agency except 097.
display_name: For each fiscal year, every vendor ID whose net under the proposed handling is $100 million or more. A row's name is recipient_parent_name when recipient_parent_uei and recipient_parent_name are both filled, and recipient_name otherwise. The display name is the name with the largest summed net on the ID's rows that year (ties broken by the name in alphabetical order).
normalized_name: Upper case, every character other than a letter, a digit or a space removed, runs of spaces collapsed to one, and the trailing words INC, INCORPORATED, CORP, CORPORATION, CO, COMPANY, LLC, LP, LTD, THE removed one at a time until the name no longer ends in one.
name_matched_split: Two or more vendor IDs with $100 million or more of net and the same normalized display name in the same year. The group's first ID is the one with the largest net. The second ID's share is the net of every ID other than the first, divided by the group's net.
first_two_words: Two vendor IDs with $100 million or more of net in the same year whose normalized names both have two or more words, share their first two words and are not equal. For review by hand, never merged.
merge_list: For each year: every name-matched split, and each of the five pairs listed by hand in every year in which both of its IDs have rows under the proposed handling, whatever their dollars. A line is marked name-matched, listed by hand, or both. Each pair listed by hand is its own line. Within a year, IDs joined by any chain of merges become one vendor, whose ID is the one with the largest net that year.
merge_effect: For each year and each set of merges (before the merges; all merges; name-matched merges only; all merges, RTX left out), every segment's HHI under the proposed handling with the merged IDs counted as one vendor, their nets summed within the segment. Reported: segments whose band differs from the band before the merges, and the share of dollars in segments with HHI above 2,500, for all agencies and for civilian agencies. The denominators are the year's net under the proposed handling, all agencies or civilian, and do not change with merges.
civilian: Every awarding agency code other than 097, the Department of Defense. A blank code counts as civilian.
va_check: Segment 036 x Q201 in FY2024. Its HHI before the merges, rounded to one decimal, must equal 6991.2. With only the two Optum IDs merged it must be 9000 or more.
candidate_pair: Two rows of the same contract_award_unique_key, as recorded (no row left out), with opposite signs, each with an absolute amount of $100,000,000 or more, whose absolute amounts differ by at most 1% of the larger. Each row is used in at most one pair. Pairs are taken in order of the smallest relative difference, then the fewest days between the rows, then the transaction keys. A pair's first row is the earlier by action date (then by key).
award_net: The sum of federal_action_obligation over every row of the award in every year in the data. total_dollars_obligated is the value on the award's row with the latest action date.
entry_error: Test A: the larger absolute amount is at least 10 times the absolute value of the award's net. Test B: the absolute amounts differ by at most 0.100% of the larger and the rows are 30 days apart or less. A pair is a likely entry error when either test marks it, and likely normal accounting otherwise. Pairs marked by only one test are listed for review.
cross_year_hhi: For each cross-year pair, the segment of each of its rows in that row's year, HHI with every row as recorded, and HHI with the pair's net on its first row and its second row set to zero.
pair_counts: The scan repeated with the minimum absolute amount set to $10,000,000, $100,000,000, $1,000,000,000, each run matched on its own.
largest_rows: The 30 rows with the largest absolute amount across all years (ties by key), with the pair each belongs to, for the explanation of the five pairs in integrity report version 3.
net_measure: A vendor's dollars in a segment are its net: the sum of its amounts under the proposed handling.
positive_only: A vendor's dollars in a segment are the sum of its positive amounts that year, returns ignored. Run 1 uses the proposed handling alone. Run 2 also nets onto its first row every same-year pair from Part 2 and every cross-year pair Part 2 marks as a likely entry error (the pair's net on its first row, its second row set to zero). Run 2 is the one to read. 'net, Part 2 pairs netted' is the net measure with the same netting, so a band change can be traced to the measure or to the netting.
unscored: A segment is unscored when no vendor has positive dollars under the measure. Split two ways: some rows with a positive amount but no vendor with positive dollars, and no row with a positive amount at all. Under positive only, the first kind cannot occur. The segments counted are those with at least one row kept under the proposed handling.
share_by_measure: The share of dollars in segments with HHI above 2,500, weighted by the measure's own dollars: the summed segment net over the year's net for net, and the summed positive dollars over the year's positive dollars for positive only. A second column weights every measure by net dollars under the proposed handling.
band_change: A segment changes band between two measures when its band (unscored included) differs.
examples: 5 segments unscored under net but scored under 'positive only, Part 2 pairs netted', the largest by positive dollars, and 5 unscored under both, the largest by negative net. Each with its 25 rows of largest absolute amount and its row count.
negative_vendor_total: A vendor's total in a segment and year under the proposed handling that is below zero. Its negative rows are its rows with a negative amount under the proposed handling.
trace: For each negative row, the award's other rows under the proposed handling with an earlier action date (strictly earlier). Earlier positive obligations are those rows with a positive amount. Reported: their dollars, the first and the most recent fiscal year with them, the fiscal years from the first of them to the row, the days from the first of them to the row, and their dollars in the row's own segment (the same awarding agency and product code, in any year).
negative_source: Each negative row falls in the first that applies: in a reversal pair from Part 2 (the scan at $100,000,000, any group); on an award with earlier positive obligations in the data; on an award with no earlier row in the data (likely older than FY2008); on an award with earlier rows but none positive.
action_type: action_type_code as recorded, labelled with the most common action_type text for the code. A blank code is labelled '(blank)'.
return_age: Fiscal years from the award's first earlier positive obligation to the negative row, in the buckets 0 years, 1 year, 2 years, 3 to 5 years, 6 to 10 years, 11 years or more, and 'no earlier positive obligation'.
terminations: The share of a year's negative dollars on rows with action_type_code E, F, X (terminate for default, for convenience, for cause). FY2025 against the mean of the yearly shares for FY2018 to FY2024.
return_awards: Awards with $1,000,000 or more of positive obligations under the proposed handling, leaving out the rows of the Part 2 pairs, whose earliest row in the data is the base record (modification number 0 or blank), so the first positive obligation falls in FY2008 or later. The stated rule (first positive obligation in FY2008 or later) holds for every award in the data, so the count under it is reported too. An award's agency, vendor and pricing type are those of its earliest row (its earliest positive row for the vendor), ties by key.
return_ratio: Returned dollars (the negative amounts, as a positive number) over positive dollars. A large return is a ratio of 50% or more. The largest return is the most negative row. Timing splits returned dollars by days from the first positive obligation: before it, 365 days or fewer, and later.
expected_share: For vendors with 10 or more such awards. The share of all such awards with a large return is taken for each awarding agency x pricing type. A vendor's expected share is the mean of those shares over its awards, and the difference is its own share minus the expected share, in percentage points. The vendor's name is the most common display name (as in Part 1) on its awards' earliest positive rows.
worked_examples: The largest negative row (by absolute amount) of each kind on an award with 40 rows or fewer: action_type_code K (close out), F (terminate for convenience), C (funding only), and a row on an award with no earlier row in the data, rows of Part 2 pairs left out; plus the largest negative vendor total in FY2025, with its rows in the segment. Award examples show up to 40 rows.
small_rows: Every row as recorded (no row left out, no pair netted). A small action is a row with an amount above zero and under $10,000. Bands: below $3,000; $3,000 to under $3,500; $3,500 to under $10,000; $10,000 and over; zero; negative; unparseable.
bunching: For each limit ($3,000, $3,500, $10,000), rows counted in $100 bins that include their upper end, (limit - 100, limit] and so on, 10 bins below the limit and 5 above. The ratio is the bin just below, (limit - 100, limit], over the bin just above, (limit, limit + 100]. Bins include their upper end because the threshold is a ceiling not to be exceeded. Rows exactly at the limit are also counted on their own, and a second ratio leaves them out of the bin just below, since round amounts gather there whatever the limit.
split_purchases: Groups of two or more rows with the same vendor, the same awarding sub-agency code and the same action date, each with an amount above zero and at or below the limit in force on its date, whose amounts sum to more than that limit. The limits follow the table in integrity report version 3: $3,000 for FY2008 to FY2015, $3,500 for FY2016 to FY2019 and for FY2020 actions before 2020-08-31, and $10,000 from 2020-08-31 and for FY2021 to FY2025. The Defense thresholds noted below that table are not applied. The vendor '(no ID)' and MISCELLANEOUS FOREIGN AWARDEES rows are left out, since neither is one vendor. 'At or below' reads the stated 'under' as within the limit, the same ceiling as for bunching. Examples: in each of FY2010, FY2014, FY2018, FY2022, FY2025, the group of 5 rows or fewer with the largest sum.
small_vendors: By year, the 10 vendors (the VENDOR expression) with the most dollars in small actions, with their share of all small-action dollars that year. Names as in Part 1.
mfa: Rows matching the MFA expression of src/analyses_v2.py (recipient_name trimmed and upper case equal to MISCELLANEOUS FOREIGN AWARDEES), every row as recorded. The check compares rows, net and share of net by year with mfa_by_year.csv of integrity report version 2, at that file's rounding.
mfa_shares: Shares of the year's rows, distinct awards (contract_award_unique_key) and net, and of the net of awarding agency 097. Segments with the placeholder hold at least one of its rows. Its share of a segment is its net over the segment's net, for segments with a positive net, counted at 10% or more and 50% or more.
mfa_countries: primary_place_of_performance_country_code, named by the most common primary_place_of_performance_country_name for the code. A blank code is '(blank)'.
mfa_high_years: The 3 years with the highest share of net are marked.
mfa_examples: In each of FY2008, FY2012, FY2016, FY2020, FY2025, the placeholder row with the largest positive amount, with its two description fields read from the Stage 1 mirror.
funding_compare: FY2011 to FY2025, every row as recorded. funding_agency_code differs when it is filled and not equal to awarding_agency_code, both as recorded. It is blank when empty after trimming. A difference in code alone can come from an agency recorded with a 3-character code in one column and a 4-character code in the other, so the rows whose codes differ but whose agency names (trimmed, upper case) match are counted too.
funding_pairs: The 15 awarding and funding code pairs with the largest net where the codes differ, over FY2011 to FY2025, named by the most common names.
funding_segments: The 50 FY2025 segments with the largest net under the proposed handling. Each one's HHI as usual, and the HHI of the segment built from the same code and product code with funding_agency_code in place of awarding_agency_code (a blank funding code is its own value). Dollars that move out: the net of the segment's rows whose funding code is not the awarding code. Dollars that move in: the net of rows funded by that code and awarded by another agency, for the same product code.
gsa_funded: The share of awarding agency 047 (General Services Administration) net, by year, on rows whose funding code is filled and not 047, and on rows whose funding code is blank.
competed: extent_competed_code in COMPETED of src/stage2.py (A, D, F, CDO), as flag X02 uses it. Every row as recorded. Dollars are net.
record_type: The first that applies: vehicle record (idv_type_code filled), order under a vehicle (parent_award_id_piid filled), definitive contract (award_type_code D), other.
offers_filled: number_of_offers_received filled means not blank after trimming. Zero means it reads as the number 0.
vehicle_join: An order joins its vehicle when the order's parent_award_id_piid equals the vehicle's award_id_piid and the order's parent_award_agency_id equals the vehicle's agency ID. No column of the vehicle record holds that ID (a sample of FY2022 orders matched awarding_sub_agency_code on 33% of rows and awarding_agency_code on almost none). It is the last part of the vehicle's contract_award_unique_key (CONT_IDV_<PIID>_<agency ID>), which always equals the first part of its contract_transaction_unique_key. A vehicle is one contract_award_unique_key, from any year in the data. The run stops if one PIID and agency ID pair belongs to more than one vehicle.
vehicle_offers: The vehicle's offers are those on its base record (modification number 0). When that is blank they come from its first row (by action date, then key) with offers filled. The zero rule applies to vehicle rows as well.
fill: A competed row's offers count as blank when blank, and when they are zero on a row before FY2012. An order's blank offers are then filled from its vehicle. Coverage is the share of competed rows and of competed dollars with offers known.
single_offer: The share of competed dollars on rows with exactly one offer, over competed dollars with offers known and over all competed dollars, for orders under single-award (S) and multiple-award (M) vehicles by parent_award_single_or_multiple_code. Before the fill uses offers as recorded, after the fill applies the zero rule and the fill.
mint_check: Orders joined to the vehicles TMHQ10C0040 and TMHQ10C0044, FY2010 to FY2025, must match the rows and net that integrity report version 3 counts.
offer_examples: In each of FY2018, FY2020, FY2022, FY2024, FY2025, the competed order row with blank offers and the largest amount whose vehicle has offers, shown with the vehicle row the count came from.
no_vendor_id: Rows whose vendor is '(no ID)' under the VENDOR expression: recipient_parent_uei and recipient_uei both blank after trimming. Every row as recorded. The agencies of a year are listed with their rows, largest first.
